boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Emerson spaces for studying, meeting, creating, playing, reflecting, and exercising, with uses and access conditions verified through current college sources.

cards.title: Reset Between Classes at Griff’s
cards.subtitle: Games and soft seating on Little Building’s second floor
cards.notes: Bring friends for pool, air hockey, foosball, arcade, Switch, or tabletop games; keep food and drinks at the room’s regular tables.
cards.short_summary: A nonreservable campus third space dedicated to casual play and downtime.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies Griff’s Game Room as a second-floor Little Building space where students can play games, relax, and connect during operating hours.
cards.access_notes: Open to Emerson students and community members during posted operational hours. Outside guests need an active Emerson sponsor and visitor registration.

cards.title: Take a Common-Facing Work Break
cards.subtitle: The main-level community lounge at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Use The Hub for an informal study session or meetup, then ask the nearby Campus Centers service desk if you need reservable space.
cards.short_summary: A community lounge for low-setup studying and conversation.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson lists The Hub as the main-level community lounge within 172 Tremont, a building offering student meeting and social spaces.
cards.access_notes: For Emerson community use; room reservations and access assistance are available through the 172 Tremont service desk.

cards.title: Prep a Meal While You Meet
cards.subtitle: A shared kitchen for casual gathering at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Plan a small meal-prep meetup here and check with Campus Centers before treating the kitchen as event space or assuming exclusive use.
cards.short_summary: A practical shared kitchen that doubles as a casual gathering place.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson describes the Community Kitchen at 172 Tremont as a space for casual gathering, meal preparation, and limited events.
cards.access_notes: Located inside 172 Tremont for the Emerson community. Limited events or reserved uses should be coordinated with Campus Centers.

cards.title: Give the Group a Formal Home Base
cards.subtitle: A presentation and workshop room at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Request this room when your group needs a defined setting for a presentation, workshop, event, or structured meeting rather than a lounge.
cards.short_summary: A reservable multipurpose setting for organized group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies the Owens Multipurpose Room at 172 Tremont as a space for formal meetings, presentations, workshops, and events.
cards.access_notes: Campus Center spaces can be requested through Spacebook; the 172 Tremont service desk can assist with booking and access.

cards.title: Find the Fourth-Floor Cultural Hub
cards.subtitle: Community space inside 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Go to the fourth floor for the Cultural Engagement Center, and consult its staff or posted programming before planning a group visit.
cards.short_summary: A specifically named cultural-engagement space within a central student building.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s current 172 Tremont page locates the Cultural Engagement Center on the building’s fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Located on the fourth floor of 172 Tremont. Program participation and room access may depend on the Center’s current schedule.

cards.title: Make Room for Reflection
cards.subtitle: Emerson’s multifaith hub at 172 Tremont
cards.notes: Use the Center’s fourth-floor setting for spiritual support or reflection; respect prayer areas and check current programming before arriving.
cards.short_summary: An inclusive multifaith campus hub with dedicated reflection facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson identifies the Center for Spiritual Life as its inclusive multifaith hub and locates it on 172 Tremont’s fourth floor with prayer and ablution space.
cards.access_notes: Campus resource for Emerson students; specific programs, support, and prayer-space use may follow posted schedules or Center guidance.

cards.title: Switch to a Quieter Setting
cards.subtitle: A focused lounge inside the Max Mutchnick Campus Center
cards.notes: Head to Piano Row’s second-floor campus center when conversation-heavy lounges are not working, and preserve the room’s quiet purpose.
cards.short_summary: A named campus-center lounge intended for quieter use.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson states that the second-floor Max Mutchnick Campus Center in Piano Row houses the Quiet Lounge.
cards.access_notes: Located within the Max Mutchnick Campus Center on Piano Row’s second floor; access follows campus-building operations.

cards.title: Reserve a Room Beyond the Classroom
cards.subtitle: A managed gathering space in Piano Row
cards.notes: Consider the Beard Room for an organized meeting or event, then request it through Spacebook instead of assuming walk-in availability.
cards.short_summary: A named campus-center room available through Emerson’s reservation system.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson lists the Beard Room inside the Max Mutchnick Campus Center and identifies it as a campus space managed by Business Services.
cards.access_notes: The Emerson community may request campus rooms through Spacebook. A reservation does not imply unrestricted public access.

cards.title: Book the Library Room Before the Meeting
cards.subtitle: Reservable study rooms managed by Iwasaki Library
cards.notes: Request a study room for focused individual or group work, and arrive on time so the space can serve the reservation as planned.
cards.short_summary: Library-managed rooms that give collaborative work a defined boundary.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson’s current space-management directory specifically lists Library Study Rooms and CoLab as spaces managed by Iwasaki Library.
cards.access_notes: Study-room use is managed by Iwasaki Library; confirm current availability and reservation requirements with the Library.

cards.title: Use the Lab That Stays Class-Free
cards.subtitle: Mac workstations and printers in Little Building 230
cards.notes: Bring computer-based work to Little Building 230 when you need a Mac or printer; verify current lab hours before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: An open-access computer lab designed for work outside scheduled classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Emerson Technology lists SBL in Little Building 230 as an open-access lab for students, faculty, and staff, with 15 Mac workstations and printers.
cards.source_title: Lab and kiosk locations and resources
cards.access_notes: Available to Emerson students, faculty, and staff during lab operating hours. Check the current technology schedule before visiting.
